The checklist (v3.0, effective 2025-03-01) lists these NPA classification checks in section B [CHK-BANK-01:B:1]:

- **Term loans:** interest or principal overdue for more than 90 days is classified as NPA [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
- **Cash credit / overdraft:** accounts that are "out of order" are classified as NPA [CHK-BANK-01:B:1]. Out of order means any of the following [CHK-BANK-01:B:1]:
  - the balance is continuously above the sanctioned limit or drawing power;
  - there are no credits for 90 days continuously as on the balance sheet date;
  - the credits are not enough to cover the interest debited in that period.
- **Bills purchased and discounted:** overdue for more than 90 days is classified as NPA [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
- **Borrower-wise classification:** if one facility of a borrower is NPA, all facilities of that borrower are NPA [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
- **Basis of classification:** it rests on the record of recovery. The security value or net worth of the borrower or guarantor is not taken into account [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
- **Year-end regularisation:** accounts regularised by one or a few credits just before year end are reviewed for inherent weakness and for reversals just after year end [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
- **Government guaranteed advances:**
  - Central Government guaranteed advances (guarantee not invoked) are treated as standard for classification but NPA for income recognition [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].
  - State Government guaranteed advances overdue more than 90 days are treated as NPA for both classification and income recognition [CHK-BANK-01:B:1].

Technical Circular 2026/03 (effective 2026-03-02, replacing CIR-2025-02) is consistent with the first five checks above. It covers the 90-day term loan and bills tests, the out-of-order test for cash credit and overdraft, borrower-wise classification, and the record-of-recovery basis [CIR-2026-03:2:1].

Section C of the checklist separately covers sub-classification and provisioning [CHK-BANK-01:C:1]. It is not part of the classification checks in section B.
